summary: Checked 79 tickers. None of last week's proposals were applied yet, so they are carried forward (ATKR, BZH, WBD acquired; PSKY is now SKYD; ESS, CME, ISRG/PRCT misfiled). New this week: Kenvue (KVUE) is gone after Kimberly-Clark closed its takeover, and Korea Electric Power (KEP) sits in Wireless Carriers but is an electric utility. About 40 strong unfiled names get homes (e.g. TBBB, NIQ, ACHC, MANH, DOCU, CROX).

moves.why: Atkore (conduit and electrical raceway) was bought by Prysmian for about $3.8B; the deal closed Oct 19, 2026 and the stock stopped trading.
Beazer Homes was acquired by Dream Finders Homes (~$2.2B); closed Oct 20, 2026 and delisted. DFH itself is the surviving homebuilder.
Warner Bros. Discovery was acquired by Paramount Skydance (merger closed early Oct 2026); its shares no longer trade. The combined company is SKYD.
Kenvue (Tylenol, Listerine, Neutrogena) was acquired by Kimberly-Clark in a ~$48.7B deal that has closed; KVUE no longer trades (last bar Oct 30).
Paramount Skydance closed its Warner Bros. Discovery merger in early October 2026 and the combined company, renamed Skydance, trades under the new ticker SKYD.
Essex Property Trust is a West Coast apartment REIT, not a battery maker (ticker mix-up with ESS Tech).
CME Group is the largest futures and options exchange (rates, equity index, energy, ags); crypto futures are a small slice. It trades with ICE/Nasdaq/CBOE.
Intuitive Surgical sells da Vinci surgical systems and instruments to hospitals; it trades like a large medtech, not an industrial robot maker.
PROCEPT BioRobotics sells the Aquablation robotic system for prostate (BPH) surgery to urologists: a medtech device company.
Nordson makes precision dispensing, fluid-management and test/inspection equipment for many industries; not a robotics company.
Rockwell Automation sells factory automation controllers, drives and software (Allen-Bradley); its natural peers are the industrial-automation group.
Lamb Weston makes frozen fries and potato products sold to restaurants and grocers; a food company, not farm equipment.
Korea Electric Power (KEPCO) is South Korea's state-controlled electric utility (generation, transmission, distribution), not a wireless carrier.
AES owns regulated utilities (AES Indiana, AES Ohio) plus a large contracted renewables/power business; it trades with defensive utilities, not rooftop solar names.

Sterling's growth engine is E-Infrastructure: site development for data centers and semiconductor fabs; it trades with the AI-buildout contractors (EME, IESC, PWR) far more than civil engineering firms.
DigitalOcean is a cloud provider for developers that now markets itself as an 'agentic inference cloud' with GPU Droplets (AMD MI350X, NVIDIA); it trades with AI-compute names.
Wabtec builds locomotives, rail equipment and transit components; it is an equipment maker, not a railroad carrier like UNP/CSX.
Legend Biotech's business is Carvykti, a CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma (with J&J); oncology is its core. Note: takeover chatter makes the chart noisy.
Zebra makes barcode scanners, rugged mobile computers and label printers for warehouses and retail (plus a small robotics unit); it is factory/warehouse automation, not surgical/industrial robots.
XP is Brazil's largest independent investment platform/broker; it trades with Brazilian/EM financials more than US brokers.
Paysign runs prepaid card programs and payment processing (pharma copay, plasma donor payments).
GRAIL sells Galleri, a blood test for multi-cancer early detection.
Lindblad Expeditions runs expedition cruises (with National Geographic) and adventure travel.
Maravai sells nucleic-acid (mRNA) production reagents and biologics safety testing to drug makers: a tools supplier.
OneSpan sells digital identity, authentication and e-signature security, mainly to banks.
Grid Dynamics provides digital engineering and AI consulting services to enterprises.
Insight Enterprises is an IT solutions integrator (hardware/software resale, cloud and AI services).
Sweetgreen is a fast-casual salad restaurant chain.
BBB Foods runs Tiendas 3B, Mexico's fast-growing hard-discount grocery chain (3,600+ stores).
NIQ (NielsenIQ) sells consumer purchase data and retail analytics to brands and retailers.
Stagwell is an advertising and marketing-services holding company (agencies plus marketing tech).
Acadia Healthcare operates behavioral-health hospitals and addiction treatment centers.
Arhaus is a premium home-furniture retailer.
Helen of Troy sells household and beauty brands (OXO, Hydro Flask, Braun, Revlon tools).
SI-BONE makes implants for sacroiliac joint and pelvic surgery.
Ceribell sells a point-of-care EEG system for detecting seizures in hospitals.
Manhattan Associates sells supply-chain and warehouse-management software.
Crocs owns the Crocs and HEYDUDE footwear brands.
DocuSign sells e-signature and agreement-management software.
SELLAS develops galinpepimut-S (WT1 cancer immunotherapy, AML) and other cancer drugs.
Eton Pharmaceuticals sells and develops treatments for rare pediatric/endocrine diseases.
Andersen Group is a tax and advisory firm that IPO'd in Dec 2025; professional services.
Climb Bio develops budoprutug, an anti-CD19 antibody for immune-mediated kidney disease (membranous nephropathy).
Vestis rents uniforms and workplace supplies (Cintas/UniFirst peer), the facility-services group.
Riskified sells AI fraud prevention and chargeback protection to e-commerce merchants.
Porch Group's main business is home insurance (reciprocal exchange) plus software for home inspectors and movers.
Septerna makes oral small-molecule GPCR drugs; its biggest program is an obesity/cardiometabolic deal with Novo Nordisk (up to $2.2B).
Xeris Biopharma sells endocrine drugs (Recorlev for Cushing's, Gvoke glucagon, Keveyis) and is growing commercially.
Ibotta runs a performance-marketing network that pays consumers cash back on brand promotions through its app and retailer partners (Walmart, Kroger): an ad platform.
Veradermics is a clinical-stage biotech developing an oral non-hormonal treatment for hair loss.
Palvella develops QTORIN topical rapamycin for rare skin diseases (microcystic lymphatic malformations); NDA submission in progress.
Cryoport provides temperature-controlled supply-chain services and equipment for cell and gene therapies: a supplier to drug makers.
PubMatic runs a sell-side ad-tech platform that helps publishers sell digital ad inventory programmatically.
BlackBerry is now mainly QNX embedded software for car systems (record QNX revenue, ~$950M backlog) plus a cybersecurity unit.
Pacira sells non-opioid pain drugs (Exparel, Zilretta, iovera) to hospitals and surgeons.
Certara sells biosimulation software and regulatory consulting used in drug development; it sits with drug-development services.
Vir Biotechnology develops antibody drugs for hepatitis delta and masked T-cell engagers for cancer.
Xometry runs an online marketplace that matches buyers with custom-manufacturing suppliers.
Royalty Pharma buys royalties on blockbuster drugs; it trades with large-cap pharma.
Anterix owns 900 MHz spectrum it leases to utilities (Oncor, Ameren, Evergy) for private LTE networks; no exact group, wireless is closest.
Hyperliquid Strategies is a crypto-treasury company holding the HYPE token (~$1.9B); it trades with the ETH treasury names (BMNR, SBET). No altcoin-treasury group exists.
Encore Capital buys and collects defaulted consumer debt (US and Europe); consumer-credit lenders are the closest group.
ChargePoint sells EV charging hardware and networked charging software; it trades with EV/clean-tech names, no exact charging group exists.
Via Transportation sells software and operations for public transit agencies (on-demand transit, routing, Citymapper); software is the closest group.
Motorola Solutions makes public-safety radios, land-mobile networks and video security; no better existing group, it just trades like a steady compounder.
Nutanix sells hyperconverged / hybrid-cloud infrastructure software, which is what this group is named for.
Johnson Controls is an HVAC and building-systems company; the current home is exact.
Oracle runs OCI, one of the big AI clouds; recent weakness is about its debt-funded capex, not a wrong group.
Infosys is the anchor of this group; moving it would empty the group.
Jacobs is an engineering, consulting and project-management firm for infrastructure and water: this group is its home.
AECOM designs and manages infrastructure projects; Engineering & Construction is the right group, the weak fit is just a quiet stock.
Axon sells Tasers, body cameras and evidence software to police; Defense Tech & Electronics is the closest group.
AppLovin runs an AI-driven mobile ad platform; current group is reasonable, it trades on its own story.
Labcorp is a diagnostic lab and drug-development services company; Genomics & Diagnostics fits.
Quest Diagnostics runs clinical lab testing; Genomics & Diagnostics fits.
TransMedics sells the Organ Care System and organ transport services; it is a medical device company, the low correlation is stock-specific.
Duolingo is a consumer language-learning app; Consumer Apps is right.
Itron makes smart meters and grid-edge networks for utilities; grid equipment is the right home.
Linde is the largest industrial gas company; the group is named for it.
